useFor: A question the reader has to answer before anything else happens: a confirmation, a short prompt, an edit that must be saved or cancelled, a first-run welcome.

combineWith.how: The answer in .modal-footer: Cancel first in the source, the confirming button last and the only filled one.
A prompt's fields in .modal-body, the whole panel in one form so Enter submits it.
What will be lost, named in the body above the question, for a destructive confirmation.
The question asked before the reader leaves a page with unsaved work is a modal of the page's own.
The receipt once the dialog has closed and the work is done.

notFor.text: A place to work that can be left without losing anything
A little detail anchored to the control that opened it
A list of actions opened from a button
Telling the reader something that needs no answer

useFor: A panel from an edge for a secondary flow that should not lose the page behind it: a record's detail, filters, a form on a phone, a sheet of actions.

combineWith.how: The filter panel moves into a start drawer on a narrow screen, opened by a Filters button with the count that applies.
A sheet's body is a list of button rows, and a record's drawer is opened from its row.
The record's history under its fields in .drawer-body, after a divider.
The record's fields as .kv rows at the top of .drawer-body.
A bottom bar's menu button opens every page of the app in a sheet.
A modal opened from inside a drawer covers it, for a confirmation of something done in the drawer.

notFor.text: A question that must be answered before anything else
A short list of actions on a pointer screen
A panel always beside the content on a wide screen
An assistant docked beside the page

useFor: Finding and running any command or page from the keyboard: type, see the matches, run one.

combineWith.how: The header search finds records with the same matcher; the palette runs commands and opens pages.
The same ranking from C# fills an empty state or a start page with the commands most likely wanted.

notFor.text: Moving between the app's pages with a pointer

useFor: Pointing the reader at one control on a page they already have open: a step of a guided tour, or a hint the first time they see something.

combineWith.how: The welcome before the reader has seen a page, the tour once they have; a step can point into an open modal.
The control a step points at is usually in a toolbar or the page head.
lock() gates hover hints for the length of a step, so two bubbles never show at once.

notFor.text: A welcome before the reader has seen the page
What a control does, on hover
Detail about a control the reader asked for
